link.note: Rockwell scrapbook (1968) identifies the house owner as Abner Smith (1734–1782), son of Aaron of The Landing; Aaron was a son of Job Smith 1st (Pelletreau pp. 44–45). Caveat (deep-dive): Pelletreau mentions more than one Abner (Aaron's son Abner p. 45; Jacob Smith's 1783 will naming brother Abner p. 50 area; 'Abner Smith, 2nd' m. Nancy dau. of Richard Smith 3rd p. 471), so the house may belong to a different Abner.

summary: John's 1st cousin 9x removed (Job → Aaron → Abner); 'an ardent patriot' whose house in the Village of the Branch is the one landmark built by John's direct Job line.
bio: Signed the Articles of Association. The 'Abner Smith House on Hauppauge Road' pictured in F. K. Smith (1967) stood on Village Way in the Village of the Branch, Smithtown ('Hauppauge Road' = old Route 111, which ends at the Branch), not in Hauppauge. Pelletreau p. 356: Capt. Richard Smith's 1736 tract was left to son Isaac in 1764 'except 10 acres which he directed to be sold', 'probably sold to Abner Smith'; the 1736 survey map marks '10 acres sold to Abner Smith' in its NE corner. In 1792 Abner's daughter Juliana quitclaimed to her brother Elisha 'all that tract of land formerly my father's Abner Smith, bounded west by the river, north and east by Wm Arthur and south by Obadiah Smith' — on the east side of the Nissequogue beside the 'Old mill creek', site of Smithtown's first mill, where relics of the old dam were visible in 1898 (pp. 44 note, 356). A first cousin of Temperance if she was James's daughter — the closest blood relative tied to any 'Hauppauge' landmark.
